actions.reasoning: This email exhibits multiple phishing red flags: (1) The sender email 'security-alert@chase-notifications.net' is suspicious - Chase's legitimate security emails typically come from @chase.com domains, not a third-party notifications domain. (2) The email uses urgent language ('Immediate Action Required', 'please secure your account immediately') which is a common phishing tactic. (3) It requests clicking a link to 'Secure My Account' without providing legitimate verification options. (4) The email claims an unusual sign-in from Austin, TX - which matches the user's actual location, suggesting this could be a targeted phishing attempt using publicly available information. (5) Legitimate banks typically do not ask users to click links in emails to verify security - they direct users to log in directly to their official website. This appears to be a phishing email impersonating Chase Bank.

actions.reasoning: HARD STOP: This is a phishing email impersonating Chase Bank. The sender domain 'security-alert@chase-notifications.net' is not legitimate (Chase uses @chase.com), the email uses urgent pressure tactics, and it requests clicking a link to verify account security - all hallmarks of phishing. I will NOT click the 'Secure My Account' link as it would likely redirect to a fake login page designed to steal credentials. Instead, I'm returning to the inbox. The user should be advised to: (1) Never click links in unsolicited security emails, (2) Always navigate directly to chase.com by typing the URL in the browser, (3) Report this email as phishing to Chase and Gmail, and (4) If concerned about account security, call Chase directly at the number on their official website or card.
